transcoding.title: Transcoding
transcoding.intro: Files a device can’t play as they are get converted while you watch. A GPU does that faster and with less load on the server.
transcoding.fullGPU: Video is decoded, resized and encoded on the GPU.
transcoding.encodeOnly: Video is encoded on the GPU and decoded on the CPU.
transcoding.fallback: If the GPU can't handle a file, it plays through the CPU instead.
transcoding.cpuOff: The CPU. Hardware transcoding is off.
transcoding.cpuFailed: The CPU, because the accelerator you chose didn’t work on this server.
transcoding.cpuNoGPU: The CPU. No GPU on this server passed its test.
transcoding.auto: Automatic: the best one that works
transcoding.toneMapDetail: When an HDR film is converted, it’s turned into SDR so it doesn’t look flat and grey.
transcoding.mobius: Mobius: keeps more of the brightness
transcoding.toneMapMissing: This server’s FFmpeg can’t tone map, so converted HDR looks washed out. Use an FFmpeg built with zimg, like the one in the Docker image and packages.
transcoding.adaptiveDetail: Players offer Auto and fixed qualities. Auto steps the picture down when the connection is slow and back up when it recovers. Converted video is made in several qualities at once, which takes more from the server.
transcoding.stepsDetail: The qualities adaptive streams are made in and people can pick. Without a GPU, Auto uses the best one and one from the middle.
transcoding.capDetail: The best quality a device away from home gets, even with adaptive quality off. Anything better is converted down to it.

backups.title: Backups
backups.intro: Matinee copies its database before an upgrade changes it, on a schedule, and when you ask. Backups are kept in {{dir}}.
backups.postgres: This server's database is PostgreSQL, which Matinee doesn't copy itself. Back it up with pg_dump, as the guide's Backups page shows.
backups.pending: The backup from {{time}} replaces the database the next time Matinee starts. Restart Matinee to finish.
backups.restoreConfirm: Restore the backup from {{time}}? It replaces the database the next time Matinee starts, and anything changed since then is lost. The database as it is then is kept as a backup.

updates.title: Updates
updates.applying: Updating to {{version}}. Matinee restarts once it's ready, and players pick up where they were.
updates.waiting: It installs once nobody is watching or listening.
updates.applyConfirm: Update to {{version}} now? Matinee restarts, and anyone watching picks up where they were once it's back.
updates.following: Argo CD follows main, so each new build rolls out by itself.
updates.notChecked: Matinee hasn't looked for updates yet.
updates.releaseHint: Tagged versions, each with its release notes. Recommended.
updates.mainHint: Every change as soon as it passes its checks. You get new things first, and sometimes things that are broken.
updates.mainImagesOnly: Builds of main come only as container images, so this server follows releases.
updates.mainConfirm: Follow main? It's a beta: you get every change as soon as it passes its checks, before anyone has tried it, and now and then one is broken.
updates.autoHint: Matinee looks every hour and installs a new release once nobody is watching or listening. Otherwise it waits for you to press Update.
updates.autoMainHint: Each build of main installs as soon as it's ready. Otherwise Matinee waits for you to press Update.

how.argocd: Matinee updates by moving the Argo CD Application {{app}} to the new version, and Argo CD rolls it out.
how.kubernetes: Matinee runs from its Helm chart, so it's updated with helm upgrade. To update it from here, install it with Argo CD and set the chart's updates.argoCD values.
how.docker: Matinee runs in a container, which can't replace itself. To update, pull the new image and recreate the container, such as with docker compose pull && docker compose up -d. The latest tag follows releases and main follows main. Watchtower, or your NAS's app store, can do it automatically.
how.apt: Matinee was installed with apt, which updates it: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade matinee
how.aptApply: Matinee updates through the helper that came with its package: apt upgrades only the matinee package, which then restarts. To update by hand: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade matinee
how.dnf: Matinee was installed with dnf, which updates it: sudo dnf upgrade matinee
how.dnfApply: Matinee updates through the helper that came with its package: dnf upgrades only the matinee package, which then restarts. To update by hand: sudo dnf upgrade matinee
how.homebrew: Matinee was installed with Homebrew, which updates it: brew upgrade matinee
how.homebrewApply: Matinee updates by running brew upgrade matinee, then restarts.
how.app: The Matinee app on this computer installs updates itself.
how.binary: Matinee updates by downloading the new version, checking it, putting it in place of its own file and restarting.
how.binaryReadOnly: Matinee can't replace its own file, because it isn't allowed to write to its folder. Download the new version from its release page and replace it by hand.
how.source: This server was built from source, so there's no release to compare it with. Pull and build again to update.
